title: Design System: The Job Order — Alberto Tuveri

title.purpose: Role lines, group headings, the signature ask. .f-role

elevation.name: rule
elevation.purpose: The ONLY elevation in the system. Fields, tables, the bench frame and every yellow region are separated by a shared 1px ink rule; there is no shadow anywhere in the build.

elevation.name: rule-soft
elevation.purpose: Hairline between rows inside one table.

elevation.name: carbon-offset
elevation.value: paper sheet offset 8px on a paper-carbon ground
elevation.purpose: The only physical depth gesture: the /work/[slug] sub-form as a carbon copy. Position and colour, never a shadow.

motion.name: ease-rule
motion.purpose: RULE-IN — a rule draws itself scaleX 0→1 from the left, then the type appears.

motion.name: ease-stamp
motion.purpose: STAMP — the rubber stamp landing, with a hair of overshoot.

motion.name: ease-sheet
motion.purpose: The route cover: a flat paper sheet rising 100%→0.

motion.name: ease-hover
motion.purpose: Hover fills, underline thickening, the readout wipe.

motion.name: dur-swap
motion.purpose: Text-state swap — a CLIP WIPE (75ms out, print, 75ms in), never an opacity fade.

motion.name: dur-text
motion.purpose: Type appearing 90ms after its rule; opacity only, no translation.

motion.name: dur-stamp
motion.purpose: STAMP impact, plus a 60ms translateY(1px) settle.

motion.name: dur-rule
motion.purpose: RULE-IN; table rows stagger 40ms under one ScrollTrigger, once:true.

motion.name: dur-print
motion.purpose: Preloader — the form printing itself; no counter, no mark.

motion.name: bench-settle
motion.purpose: The bench holds its captured still until the sample has settled, then cross-fades to the live frame over 320ms and stamps LIVE.

motion.name: never-animated
motion.value: numbers · body copy · the bench canvas · the yellow regions
motion.purpose: A printed value is final at first paint: no count-up, no reel, no transform on the canvas.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Rules born drawn, all six stamps already impressed, cover replaced by a 150ms swap, bench = labelled still. Local feedback swaps stay.

z.name: z-bench
z.purpose: The canvas inside the bench frame.

z.name: z-band
z.purpose: Sticky phase band and header strip.

geometry.name: bench
geometry.purpose: Unitless aspect-ratio so the box reserves its space: CLS 0.

geometry.name: readout-column
geometry.purpose: The yellow instrument column beside the bench; a full-width strip below it on mobile.

geometry.name: perforation
geometry.value: 1px dotted ink + two 6px punched holes at the margins
geometry.purpose: Between sections; drawn in CSS, the only radial-gradient in the stylesheet.

budget.name: renderers
budget.purpose: The bench on / is the only heavy renderer on the site.

budget.name: particles
budget.purpose: The readout prints the real count after tiering.

budget.name: dpr-cap
budget.purpose: Applied to the canvas backing store; the readout prints what was applied.

budget.name: axe
budget.purpose: 7 routes × 2 viewports, plus the reduced-motion and no-WebGPU variants.

components.name: Field
components.description: The captioned ruled box every element of the sheet is made of. Draws top and left only; the grid closes right and bottom, so touching fields never double a line.

components.name: Phase cell (stamped)
components.description: One of the six cells of the sticky yellow band. Stamped on entry with the STAMP verb; the role tag prints in ink beneath it.

components.name: Bench readout
components.description: One row of the yellow instrument column. Every value is read from the engine; a value it has not produced prints an em dash. The 500ms refresh is a 150ms clip wipe, never an opacity fade.
components.css: .ds-readouts { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 112px; min-width: 112px; margin: 0; background: var(--color-safety, #ffc400); color: var(--color-ink, #141414); border: 1px solid var(--color-ink, #141414); border-left: 0; } .ds-readouts > div { padding: 8px 12px; } .ds-readouts .ds-rule { border-top: 1px solid rgb(20 20 20 / .22); } .ds-readouts dt { font-size: .75rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px; font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 87; } .ds-readouts dd { margin: 0; font-size: .9375rem; line-height: 24px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 87; clip-path: inset(-12% var(--wr, 0%) -12% var(--wl, 0%)); }

components.name: Link
components.description: The only link treatment on paper: stamp red, 1px underline at 3px offset thickening to 2px in 120ms. There is no button component in this world.
components.css: .ds-link { color: var(--color-stamp, #b40f29); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 3px; font-size: .9375rem; transition: text-decoration-thickness 120ms linear; } .ds-link:hover, .ds-link:focus-visible { text-decoration-thickness: 2px; } .ds-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-safety, #ffc400); outline-offset: 1px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-ink, #141414); border-radius: 0; }

components.name: Perforation
components.description: The tear line between sections: a dotted ink rule with a 6px punched hole at each margin. Pure CSS, the only radial-gradient in the stylesheet.
components.css: .ds-perf { position: relative; height: 8px; margin-block: 8px; border-top: 1px dotted var(--color-ink, #141414); } .ds-perf::before, .ds-perf::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: -4px; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at center, var(--color-paper-carbon, #dcd9cf) 0 1.6px, var(--color-ink, #141414) 1.8px 3px, transparent 3.2px); } .ds-perf::before { left: 0; } .ds-perf::after { right: 0; }

narrative.overview:
The site is one printed job order on workshop paper. Everything on it is a field with a stamped caption, a measured value and a provenance cell — employer, date, link — and the only thing alive on the sheet is the engineer's own GPU fluid, running inside a framed test bench with the frame time printed in the margin beside it. The form is not a costume: it comes from Maintech OMA, the workshop ERP the owner founded, whose six-phase state machine — Intake · Diagnosis · Estimate · Work · Test · Release — is also the visitor's path down the page. The sticky yellow phase band accumulates rubber stamps as you scroll, one per region, counting 1 / 6 to 6 / 6, and it never un-stamps: a job card only fills up.

The density is documentary, not editorial. Fields share their rules instead of repeating them, tables are hairlines, numerals are tabular everywhere a figure appears, and structure — rows, rules, perforations, stamps — is the page's only ornament. There is one typeface at four widths, no shadow anywhere, no gradient, no glass, no monospace costume, no dark section. Yellow is a region, never a stripe: the band, the instrument column and the signature panel together are about a third of the surface, and that commitment is what makes the page recognisable with every word removed.

What this world refuses is as load-bearing as what it does: the near-black hero with a giant name and a blob on the cursor, the logo bento, the 'Selected Works' grid with hover-reveal, and the white typographic list that is its mirror image. Nothing here is decorative, and nothing is claimed that is not measured.
keyCharacteristics: Workshop paper and safety yellow, with stamp red reserved for stamps, links and arrows.
One family — Archivo variable — read at four widths: 125 / 112 / 100 / 87 / 75.
Flat by direction: a single 1px ink rule is the only elevation in the system.
Every fact carries a provenance cell; every hole is printed as a field, never as a placeholder.
Two motion verbs, RULE-IN and STAMP, and numbers that never animate.

rules.name: The Region Rule
rules.body: Yellow is only ever a whole region with its own 1px ink border — band, instrument column, signature cell, Release panel. If a yellow shape is thinner than the thing it contains, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Yellow Rule
rules.body: Secondary text on yellow is ink, never graphite: #5a5a57 on #ffc400 is 4.33:1 and is a forbidden pair. /styleguide prints both forbidden pairs with their computed ratio and a FAIL verdict, at large-text scale so the specimen itself is not a violation.

rules.name: The Filled Stamp Rule
rules.body: A stamp on the yellow band is filled red with paper lettering. There is no outlined red stamp anywhere in the build.

rules.name: The One Material Rule
rules.body: Never add a second family or a monospace. If a run of text needs to read differently, move it on the width axis (125 / 112 / 100 / 87 / 75), not to another typeface.

rules.name: The Printed Name Rule
rules.body: The name is printed, not assembled: no SplitText, no per-character reveal, no count-up. The rule above it draws, and the type is simply there.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose caps at var(--measure) (68ch), cells at 44ch, the lead at 58ch. A scan list may take the sheet measure but never exceed it.

rules.name: The Shared Rule Rule
rules.body: Two touching fields share one 1px line. If you can see a 2px line anywhere, a field is drawing a border the grid already closed.

rules.name: The One Renderer Rule
rules.body: One heavy renderer exists on the whole site — the bench on /. Every other route mounts no canvas at all.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No shadow, no blur, no glass, no gradient — the only radial-gradient in the stylesheet draws the 6px perforation punch-hole. If a surface needs to read as lifted, give it a rule, not a shadow.

dos: Do print every fact with a provenance cell — employer · date · link — and every hole as a field ('no photograph on file', 'URL: pending', 'not in the catalogue').
Do keep yellow as a whole region with its own ink border, at roughly a third of the surface.
Do read text from src/content/dict.ts (zod-validated, EN ≡ IT). No visible string is ever written in a component.
Do use tabular-nums lining-nums wherever a figure appears, and let the arrow — never a colour — say the direction of a delta.
Do move on the width axis (125 / 112 / 100 / 87 / 75) when text needs to read differently.
Do keep the two motion verbs. A new interaction is expressed as a rule drawing or a stamp landing, or it is not expressed.
Do give every degraded state a printed reason on a known ground ('Renderer not available on this device'), and label the still frame it shows.
donts: Don't add a shadow, gradient, glass, blur, dark section, monospace face, icon card, kicker over a heading that is not a real field caption, or a gradient-filled letterform.
Don't animate a number, the body copy, the canvas, or a yellow region.
Don't put text over the fluid; the caption is above the frame and the readouts are beside it.
Don't cross-fade text through opacity on a coloured ground — wipe it.
Don't put graphite on yellow (4.33:1) or an outlined red stamp on yellow (3.68:1).
Don't add a z-index that is not one of the seven in the scale, or a colour that is not one of the eleven.
Don't mount a second heavy renderer; the bench on / is the only one.
Don't print a figure that is not in PRODUCT.md §3/§9 — node scripts/check-claims.mjs is the gate.
Don't ship a raster without embedded provenance (impeccable embed-prompt --scan public/...).
